meta.name: OpenCAWR — Car Analysis / What's it Really cost
meta.basis: drive-to-death lifetime cost per mile; user profile: 13k mi/yr, USAA active-duty, Florida reg, Fresno CA garaging
meta.provenance_note: Established vehicles use hand-curated price-vs-odometer curves anchored to real cars.com/iSeeCars pulls. Reliability tiers were RE-DERIVED 2026-07-29 from NHTSA complaint data alone (public domain, keyless) per docs/reliability-methodology.md. eol_maintained_miles was RE-DERIVED 2026-07-31 from New York State DMV vehicle-inspection data (public, keyless, no licence conditions) per docs/eol-methodology.md, replacing the lost prototype's 'iSeeCars empirical × 1.30 maintained bonus' longevity judgment — no field here derives from iSeeCars any more. repair_cost_multiplier_by_make is 1.0 for every non-'sport' row, a deliberate negative result: no public per-make repair-cost source exists. With all three re-derived, spec §9 clause 1 (Consumer Reports) is CLOSED for the seed set and no CR, CarComplaints or RepairPal data is used anywhere; clause 2 (scraped listing data) still governs the price curves above and remains OPEN. The 2 'sport' rows are an owner carve-out and are never derived. Both derivations are coarse and carry real limitations — the reliability tier is complaint MIX, not a measured defect rate, and eol_maintained_miles mixes durability with NY owner mileage by design and is a single-state sample; read each methodology's 'Known limitations' before quoting a number. Vehicles in 'proxied' were estimated from segment peers (no used history).
